title: Claim DTAA Benefits: How to Apply for Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) using Form 42

faq.q: What is a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)?
faq.a: A DTAA is a tax treaty between two countries designed to prevent individuals and entities from being taxed twice on the same income earned across borders. It provides mechanisms for relief, such as exemptions or tax credits.

faq.q: Who needs a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)?
faq.a: Any Indian tax resident earning income from a foreign country with which India has a DTAA, and wishing to claim benefits under that DTAA, needs a TRC.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) apply for TRC from India?
faq.a: No, a TRC is issued to certify tax residency in India. NRIs are not tax residents of India, so they cannot apply for an Indian TRC. They would need a TRC from their country of residence if they wish to claim DTAA benefits there.

faq.q: What documents are typically needed for Form 42?
faq.a: You will need your PAN, details of your residential status and address, the specific financial year for which the TRC is required, and information about the foreign country and the income earned there.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a TRC after applying?
faq.a: The processing time can vary, but typically, the Income Tax Department issues the TRC within a few weeks of a complete and correctly filed online application. It's advisable to apply well in advance.

faq.q: Is a TRC valid for multiple countries or income streams?
faq.a: An Indian TRC certifies your tax residency in India for a specific financial year. You can use this single TRC to claim DTAA benefits with any country with which India has a DTAA, for all eligible income streams.

faq.q: What if my foreign income is small?
faq.a: Even if your foreign income is small, if it is subject to taxation in both countries, obtaining a TRC and claiming DTAA benefits can help you avoid double taxation and potentially reduce your overall tax liability.

fact_check.summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding DTAA benefits and the application process for a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) using Form 42 in India, though some references to the Income-tax Act of 1961 are outdated as it has been replaced by the Income-tax Act, 2025.
